compose      You are authoring a HyperFrames composition — deterministic HTML/CSS/GSAP that renders
compose      frame by frame to video.
compose      Read CONTRACT.md and BRIEF.md in this directory first. The contract is binding.
compose      Write exactly three files: index.html, styles.css, animation.js. Nothing else.
compose      The bar is not that it validates. It is that the eight rendered frames read as eight
compose      structurally different compositions. Six variations of one layout is a failure.

compose      You are authoring a **HyperFrames composition** — real HTML, CSS and GSAP that renders
compose      deterministically to video, frame by frame, in headless Chrome.
compose      You will be given: a `plan.json`, a generated `tokens.css`, a set of block stylesheets,
compose      a reference exemplar, and a working directory. You write three files into that directory:
compose      styles.css      scene-specific styling (imports nothing; blocks are linked separately)
compose      animation.js    one paused GSAP timeline
compose      Everything else in the directory is provided and must not be modified.
compose      ## 1. Hard framework rules — violating any of these produces a broken render
compose         `data-duration`, `data-fps`. **These are pre-filled in the scaffold — do not change them.**
compose      2. Every timed element needs **all four**: `class="clip"`, `data-start`, `data-duration`,
compose         `data-track-index`. Seconds, not milliseconds. An element missing `class="clip"` will
compose         not be hidden outside its window.
compose      3. The timeline must be **paused** and registered:
compose         The renderer seeks this timeline per frame. A timeline that plays itself renders wrong.
compose      4. **Deterministic only.** No `Date.now()`, no `Math.random()`, no `fetch`, no remote
compose         fonts, images, scripts or stylesheets. Everything is local and already present.
compose      5. Audio is a single `<audio class="clip">` element pointing at the provided narration.
compose         Videos use `muted` plus a separate `<audio>` if they carry sound.
compose      6. Animate with GSAP only — its clock is seekable. CSS `@keyframes` animations are not
compose         frame-accurate under seek and will render as frozen or wrong.
compose         `strokeDashoffset`. Set `transformOrigin` explicitly whenever you scale or rotate.
compose      8. **Nothing may sit completely still for more than one second.** After a scene's
compose         entrance finishes it must keep moving — a slow drift, a growing rule, a rotating
compose         mark, a staggered late reveal. A held still frame reads as a stall to a viewer and
compose         fails the freeze check, which no amount of passing `check` will save.
compose         **What moves has to have area.** The check averages the change across the whole
compose         frame, so a hairline crossing a 1080×1920 canvas alters a few thousand pixels out of
compose         two million and counts as nothing at all. A field, a card, a large mask, a counting
compose         figure, a shifting block of colour: those register. A one-pixel rule does not, however
compose         far it travels — this is measured, and a full-duration `.signal-spine` on its own has
compose         already failed it. BRIEF.md gives you, per scene, the longest stretch in which the
compose         caption layer changes nothing; in those stretches your motion is the only thing in the
compose         picture, and it is sampled **before** the video is rendered, not after.
compose         **And that mass goes behind the type, or beside it. Never across it.** These two
compose         sentences are one rule, and taking only the first is a failure with its own check:
compose         `layout: Text is hidden beneath an opaque element`. The first composition written
compose         against the paragraph above drew twenty of them in one pass, because "move something
compose         large" was read as licence to sweep an opaque card over a headline.
compose         So: give the moving mass a lower `data-track-index` than any text it overlaps, or
compose         keep it in a region the text does not occupy, or make it translucent enough to read
compose         through — an `rgba(0,0,0,α)` or `rgba(255,255,255,α)` scrim at α ≤ 0.5 is not opaque
compose         and does not trip this. A wipe that reveals type is fine; a wipe that buries it is not.
compose         If you cannot tell which you have built, you have built the second one.
compose      9. **Never hardcode a scene's time in `animation.js`. Read it from the DOM.**
compose         Position every scene-local tween as `at("#scene-x") + offset`, and derive anything
compose         that runs to the end of a scene from `len("#scene-x")`. Only the composition's own
compose         total duration may be read once from the root element.
compose         This is not a style preference. The owner edits copy and pacing directly in the
compose         plan, which shifts every later scene; if your timings are literals the picture and
compose         the narration drift apart on the very next edit, and fixing it costs a full
compose         re-author. Reading from the DOM makes those edits free and correct.
compose      10. **The same goes for the canvas size. Never write a pixel dimension as a literal.**
compose          timeline.fromTo(".spine-node", {y: 0}, {y: HEIGHT, duration: TOTAL, ease: "none"}, 0);
compose          **One composition serves every format in its family**, re-emitted at a different
compose          root size: portrait is 1080×1920, 1080×1350 and 1080×1080. A `1920` written into
compose          `animation.js` is right in the one format you happened to picture and wrong in the
compose          other two, where the element travels off the canvas and stays there. This is
compose          checked, and it is an error.
compose          Better still, reach for units that need no number at all — `cqw` / `cqh`,
compose          percentages, and the `--u` scale variable adapt on their own.
compose      `tokens.css` is linked first and defines every colour you may use, as `var(--brand-*)`.
compose      - **Never write a hex, `rgb()` or `hsl()` colour literal in `styles.css`.**
compose      - The only exceptions are neutral scrims: `rgba(0,0,0,α)` and `rgba(255,255,255,α)`.
compose      - A rogue colour literal is a **hard failure** and the composition is rejected.
compose      - Only use foreground/background combinations listed in the plan's approved contrast
compose        pairs. Inventing a pair will fail the WCAG contrast pass.
compose      ## 3. Plan conformance — this is what makes the video re-editable
compose      The plan is the durable artefact; your composition is keyed to it.
compose      - One top-level `<section class="scene clip">` per plan section, with
compose        Use the exact numbers from the plan. Do not re-time anything — the timings come from
compose        measured narration audio and are already correct.
compose      - **Every `section.onScreen` string must appear verbatim in that section's DOM text.**
compose        You may split it across elements and wrap parts in `<em>` or `<span>`, but the
compose        concatenated text content must contain the string exactly, including punctuation.
compose        Do not paraphrase, do not translate, do not change case via text (use CSS for that).
compose      - Do not invent additional copy that makes claims. Decorative labels ("ANGLE", "MON",
compose        "STATUS") are fine; new factual statements are not.
compose - If a section has `mediaId`, render `` (or `
compose        a clip). The real file is copied in under that exact name. Never invent a path.
compose      - If a section has `slot`, render `<div class="presenter-slot style-<slot.style>"
compose        data-placeholder-label="PRESENTER — Ns">` sized and positioned for a person.
compose        Do not put a `<video>` inside it — the assembler binds media later.
compose      - The composition serves several canvas sizes in the same family. **Lay out with flow,
compose        not absolute top offsets.** `.scene` is a three-row grid (masthead / body / footer);
compose        put your content in `<div class="scene-body">`.
compose        Absolute pixel values are acceptable only for hairlines, dots and small fixed marks.
compose      - **`--gutter` is the content inset and the left edge of everything readable.** The strip
compose        between the canvas edge and `--gutter` is a reserved lane: it carries the full-height
compose        spine at `--spine-x` and nothing else. Never position copy, a label or the logo as a
compose        fraction of the gutter — that is how they end up flush against a moving accent line.
compose      - The bottom caption band is reserved by `.scene` padding. **Never place copy there.**
compose      - `position: absolute` inside a scene is fine when anchored to an edge or a percentage —
compose        just never to a hardcoded vertical pixel offset.
compose      - Add `data-layout-allow-overflow` to any element that intentionally bleeds off-canvas,
compose        otherwise the layout check flags it.
compose      Linked before your `styles.css`. Use them; do not reimplement them.
compose      | `brand-rail.css` | `.brand-rail`, `.brand-seal`, `.rail-rule` | **mandatory** — one, full duration, high tra
compose      | `cta-lockup.css` | `.cta-lockup`, `.cta-seal`, `.cta-url` | **mandatory when the plan has a `cta` section**
compose      | `presenter-slot.css` | `.presenter-slot` | required when a section has a slot |
compose      **One continuous element is mandatory.** Include `.signal-spine` — or an equivalent of
compose      your own design — as a full-duration clip on a low track, animated across the entire
compose      composition (the spine's line grows and its node travels). It carries the brand's "one
compose      thread through the whole piece" rule.
compose      It does **not** satisfy §1.8 on its own. A spine is a hairline, and the freeze measure
compose      averages change across the whole frame: compositions carrying a perfectly good spine have
compose      frozen anyway, because a line one pixel wide changes too little of the canvas to count.
compose      The spine is the thread; the motion with area is a separate thing each scene needs.
compose      Add `.on-light` to `.brand-rail`, `.kicker`, `.section-number` and `.rule` when they sit
compose      on a light field; `.on-dark` to `.cta-lockup` when it sits on the dark field.
compose      ### 5a. Screenshots, and moving through them
compose      When a section carries a `screen` block, the brief gives you the file, the chrome and a
compose      list of focus rects with times. The shot is real product evidence — never redraw it, never
compose      fake a UI, never crop it to hide something.
compose      To move to a focus rect whose fraction of the image is `x, y, w, h`:
compose        scale: 1 / Math.max(w, h),   // the rect fills the stage's shorter axis
compose      Set `transformOrigin` on the same tween, not before it. Left at its default the frame
compose      drifts toward the middle of the image no matter which detail it was aimed at, which is the
compose      one failure that looks deliberate and is not.
compose      **A full-page screenshot at stage size teaches nothing.** If a section talks about a
compose      control, the frame has to arrive at that control. A shot held whole for eight seconds while
compose      the narration describes a detail inside it is a failed scene even though every check passes.
compose      When a section carries a `data` block, the brief gives you labels, values, a unit and a
compose      suggested shape. **The shape is a suggestion.** Four values might be bars, or one enormous
compose      figure with three small ones under it, or a single count-up — pick what suits the scene you
compose      are building, and do not let a chart become the only thing in the frame.
compose      Two things are not negotiable:
compose      - **Animate the arrival.** `.data-bar > span` grows by tweening `--fill` from 0 to 1; a
compose        `.data-figure` counts up. A chart that cuts in at its final value has no reason to be a
compose      - **Render the source note** in `.data-source`. The brief gives you the text. A figure on
compose        screen with no attribution is not something anyone can cite, and you cannot invent one.
compose      Never state a figure the brief did not give you, and never round one to look neater.
compose      ## 6. The rule that actually decides whether this is any good
compose      **Every scene must be a structurally different composition.**
compose      This is the single failure mode that matters. A sequence of six centred cards with
compose      different text is a failed video even when every check passes. The frames of a good
compose      piece are recognisably different from each other at thumbnail size.
compose      Give each scene a distinct spatial archetype. Pick from — and extend — ideas like:
compose      - one enormous headline with everything else stripped away
compose      - a paper artefact at an angle, with fragments scattered around it
compose      - two columns with a transformation mark between them
compose      - a vertical spine with staggered entries hanging off it
compose      - a full-bleed colour field where the palette inverts entirely
compose      - a single object dead-centre with concentric rings

compose      - `media/logo-lockup-dark.png` — **lockup**, for dark fields, 1040×192, clear space 25%. Seal, wordmark and ta

compose      **Every scene must be a structurally different composition.**
compose      This is the single failure mode that matters. A sequence of six centred cards with
compose      different text is a failed video even when every check passes. The frames of a good
compose      piece are recognisably different from each other at thumbnail size.
compose      Give each scene a distinct spatial archetype. Pick from — and extend — ideas like:
compose      - one enormous headline with everything else stripped away
compose      - a paper artefact at an angle, with fragments scattered around it
compose      - two columns with a transformation mark between them
compose      - a vertical spine with staggered entries hanging off it
compose      - a full-bleed colour field where the palette inverts entirely
compose      - a single object dead-centre with concentric rings
compose      - a corner-anchored lockup with a hairline running to the opposite edge
compose      - a horizontal band across the middle with the canvas empty above and below
compose      Vary these axes across the sequence: **where the mass sits** (left / right / centre /
compose      edge), **the dominant shape** (type / card / line / circle / field), **the background**
compose      (paper / white / accent / the rare inverse field), and **the direction of motion**
compose      (in from the left / up from below / scale from centre / wipe from the bottom).
compose      Two adjacent scenes must never share an archetype. If your composition would render six
compose      variations of one layout, throw it away and start again — that is exactly the outcome

compose      stagger is the motion equivalent of six identical cards.
